Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: Mobile money operators and NatSwitch generate revenue from the digital payment system. NatSwitch operates on a cost-recovery/not-for-loss basis with joining fees, annual membership fees, and interchange fees on all transactions. Airtel Money and TNM Mpamba generate revenue from transaction fees, float income, and value-added services. GSMA data shows average revenue per mobile money user in Sub-Saharan Africa was $3.51 in 2024, with ~80% of providers operating EBITDA-positive. The RBM Q3 2024 NPS report shows K10.4 trillion in mobile money transaction value, indicating significant commercial activity. Revenue-generating capacity of the payment system is well established.

Definition: Whether an official government web portal or mobile application exists where taxpayers can file tax returns and pay taxes online with direct e-payment capability linked to instant payment system.
Comments: The Malawi Revenue Authority (MRA) operates Msonkho Online (also called ITAS - Integrated Tax Administration System), a fully live digital tax portal allowing taxpayers to register, file tax returns (PAYE, VAT, excise, income tax), make payments, and manage tax compliance. The EIS (Electronic Invoicing System) was introduced in 2026 as an additional e-invoicing compliance layer. The MRA portal has an EIS Portal (eis-portal.mra.mw) for taxpayer services. Msonkho Online won the 2025 ICTAM award. The front-end modules (registration, filing, payment, objections) are fully operational, though back-end audit modules were still being completed as of 2023.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports business payments to suppliers, vendors, contractors, and other businesses for commercial transactions, procurement, and supply chain payments.
Comments: Business-to-business (B2B) payments are supported in Malawi. MITASS processes large-value interbank and business payments (accounting for 73.3% of total transaction value in Q3 2024). NatSwitch supports B2B payments via real-time EFT (since 2022) and internet banking (298,750 subscribers as of Q3 2024). The AfricaNenda SIIPS 2023 report and PaymentComponents confirm NatSwitch supports B2B use cases. NatSwitch is also planning to develop an e-commerce service to further facilitate B2B payments.

Definition: Whether the system enables consumer payments to merchants and businesses for goods and services, including retail purchases, bill payments, e-commerce, and subscription services.
Comments: Person-to-business (P2B) payments are operational in Malawi. Mobile money supports bill payments (utilities 24%, goods and services 15% per FinScope 2023). NatSwitch facilitates P2B payments via POS (live since 2016) and real-time EFT (2022). Business Licensing Regulations (2019) mandate that licensed businesses must offer at least one electronic payment channel. PayChangu (2021) offers merchant APIs. The AfricaNenda SIIPS report and PaymentComponents confirm NatSwitch supports P2B use cases. USSD-based merchant payments are common.

Definition: Whether the system enables citizen payments to government for taxes, fees, licenses, fines, utility bills, and other government service charges.
Comments: Person-to-government (P2G) payments are in active use in Malawi. The Malawi Revenue Authority (MRA) operates Msonkho Online (its Integrated Tax Administration System / ITAS), which allows taxpayers to register, file returns, and pay taxes online. The MRA EIS Portal is a live taxpayer portal. Utility and government service payments via mobile money are active (FinScope 2023 shows 24% of mobile money users pay utilities). Business Licensing Regulations (2019) mandated businesses to accept electronic payments including for government fee payments. NatSwitch also plans an e-gateway for P2G payments.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports direct person-to-person transfer of funds between individuals for informal transactions, remittances, and interpersonal value transfers.
Comments: Person-to-person (P2P) payments are well established and widely used in Malawi. Both Airtel Money and TNM Mpamba support P2P transfers and have done so since 2012. NatSwitch enables interoperable P2P transfers between different networks (live for ATM 2015, then EFT in 2022). The RBM has actively promoted P2P by scrapping or reducing inter-network transfer fees. FinScope 2023 shows 'send and receive money' (89%) and 'to send money to someone else's account' (59%) are the top mobile money use cases.

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: The Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM) directly operates MITASS (the Malawi Interbank Transfer and Settlement System) — the largest payment system in the country — and acts as the sole settlement agent for all interbank payments. Under the Payment Systems Act No. 15 of 2016, the RBM holds full regulatory and oversight authority over all payment, clearing and settlement systems. The RBM also directly participated in establishing NatSwitch (with World Bank FSTAP funding) and mandated all PSPs to connect to it via the 2017 Interoperability Directive. The RBM's 2024 Annual Report confirms it operates MITASS and the Automated Clearing House. This constitutes direct operation of core payment infrastructure.

Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: Consumer protection in digital payments is partial in Malawi. The Competition and Fair Trading Commission (CFTC) has a mandate on consumer protection including for mobile money services. The Electronic Transactions and Cybersecurity Act (2016) includes consumer rights provisions for e-commerce transactions (cooling-off periods, cancellation rights). The RBM issued a draft Financial Consumer Protection Bill in 2024 to strengthen the legal framework, but this was still in draft form as of mid-2024. The RBM's Mobile Payment System Guidelines (2011/2014) include basic consumer protection requirements. A dedicated comprehensive Financial Consumer Protection law has not yet been enacted, making this partial.

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: Data breach notification is mandatory in Malawi under the Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2024 (effective June 3, 2024). Section 33 requires data processors to notify their engaging entity within 72 hours of a breach, and data controllers must notify MACRA within 72 hours if the breach is likely to risk rights and freedoms of individuals. MACRA issued draft Guidelines on Data Breach Notifications to clarify the scope, timing, and content of required notifications. This constitutes a mandatory notification regime.

Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: Malawi has specific payment data provisions under multiple laws. The Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2024 (effective June 3, 2024) provides a comprehensive framework for personal data protection including financial data, mandatory breach notification, data subject rights, and MACRA as the enforcement authority. Earlier, the Electronic Transactions and Cybersecurity Act No. 33 of 2016 included basic data protection provisions for electronic transactions. The Payment Systems Act (2016) and Mobile Payment System Guidelines also contain data security requirements. The 2024 DPA specifically applies to payment data processed by mobile money operators and banks.

Definition: Whether payment system operators or regulators regularly publish performance metrics and statistics on system usage, transaction volumes/values, participant numbers, uptime, and other operational indicators.
Comments: The Reserve Bank of Malawi publishes quarterly National Payment Systems (NPS) Reports that include detailed statistics on mobile money subscribers, transaction volumes and values, MITASS activity, NatSwitch transactions, internet banking, and key performance metrics. These reports are publicly available and referenced in media (e.g. Q3 2024, Q2 2025 reports). The RBM also publishes annual financial statements that include payment system performance data. This constitutes regular quarterly/monthly reporting.

Definition: Whether payment system governance explicitly includes mechanisms to ensure inclusivity and represent interests of vulnerable populations, including provisions for input from all participant types, consumer representatives, small providers, or explicit financial inclusion mandates in governance documents.
Comments: There is partial pro-poor governance in Malawi's payment system. The National Payments Council (NPC) includes government representation (Ministry of Finance Accountant General) but is primarily composed of banks and financial institutions. The RBM initiated a Scale-up and Regulation of Electronic Payments project (2021) with AFI and Mastercard Foundation, and Business Licensing Regulations mandate all licensed businesses to offer electronic payment options. There is no dedicated consumer representative body formally embedded in NatSwitch governance. The SCTP e-payment transition (2022) demonstrates government effort to include ultra-poor households, but formal pro-poor governance representation in payment scheme decision-making bodies is partial rather than systematic.

Definition: Whether the scheme rules governing payment system participation, pricing structure, technical requirements, security standards, and conduct are publicly accessible via website, public repository, or on request. Transparency indicator.
Comments: NatSwitch scheme rules are partially available. The 2017 Retail Payment System Interoperability Directive (which mandated PSP connection to NatSwitch) was published in the Malawi Gazette. The Payment Systems Act No. 15 of 2016 is publicly available on MalawiLII. However, detailed NatSwitch operating guidelines, fee schedules, and interchange rules are not fully public — the AfricaNenda SIIPS 2023 report notes the exact interchange fee amounts 'are not publicly available'. The RBM publishes directives and guidelines for PSPs on request or via gazette, making information partially available on request rather than fully public.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: Malawi has a fully deployed nationwide digital payment system. The National Switch (NatSwitch/NatSwitch Ltd) connects all banks and mobile money operators (MMOs) and has been operational since 2015 (ATM), 2016 (POS), and 2022 (real-time EFT). The system is complemented by MITASS (Malawi Interbank Transfer and Settlement System), mobile money platforms Airtel Money and TNM Mpamba (both live since 2012), and an extensive agent network. By 2022, NatSwitch was processing EFT transfers in real time and the ecosystem covered ATMs, POS, mobile money, internet banking, and USSD channels. The FinScope 2023 survey found 69% of adults use mobile money and 88% are financially included.

Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: Active user penetration is in the 20-49% range. FinScope Consumer Survey 2023 found 69% of adults 'use mobile money' but only 54% own a registered mobile money account. However, 'use' includes over-the-counter (OTC) usage. The 30-day activity rate for registered mobile money subscribers was 40-43% as of 2025 (RBM Q2 2025 NPS Report), and the 90-day rate was 52-56%. The AfricaNenda SIIPS 2023 survey found only 40% of sampled Malawians made or received a digital payment in the year prior (classifying Malawi as 'emerging'). The Nation Online (2025) reported mobile money penetration 'below 45%'. The Global Findex 2021 showed ~20% of Malawi adults had a mobile money account. Combining evidence, active regular users (30-day basis) are in the 20-49% range of all adults.

Definition: Whether independent external audits of payment system security, operations, financial controls, and compliance are conducted by third-party auditors, and whether audit results or summaries are made public.
Comments: The Reserve Bank of Malawi publishes audited annual financial statements (its 2024 financial statements were audited by external auditors and published). The RBM operates under IMF/World Bank program oversight that includes assessment of payment system governance. NatSwitch Ltd operates with financial audits as part of its corporate governance. However, dedicated public audits specifically of the national payment system operations are not prominently published. The RBM financial statement audits are public (available on Scribd). Private/internal audits of MITASS and NatSwitch are conducted but not publicly reported as standalone payment system audits.

Definition: Whether digital payment systems and access points (apps, USSD, agents) are designed to accommodate persons with disabilities (visual, hearing, mobility, cognitive impairments), and disability-disaggregated coverage rates if data available.
Comments: There is no systematic disability-accessible design in Malawi's digital payment system. The primary channel is USSD (text-based, not accessible to visually impaired or those with low literacy), with SIM Toolkit as secondary. The IDinsight 2024 SCTP e-payment study specifically identified that 'people with disabilities face challenges traveling long distances to mobile money agents' due to mobility issues, and noted access challenges for elderly, disabled, and chronically ill SCTP beneficiaries as a key concern. There are no known screen-reader-compatible apps or specific accessibility features for the payment system. No formal regulatory accessibility standards have been established for digital payments in Malawi.

Definition: Percentage of government payments (G2P disbursements including salaries, pensions, social transfers) made through instant digital payment system rather than cash or check, reflecting government adoption and modernization.
Comments: Government adoption of digital payments for its own disbursements remains below 20% of all government payment flows. While the SCTP e-payment rollout was underway in 10+ districts by mid-2024 (out of 28 total), as of 2023 the majority of SCTP districts still used manual cash payments. The Integrated Financial Management Information System (IFMIS) roll-out to all 28 Ministries, Departments and Agencies was completed in 2021 but World Bank assessments note most MDAs 'are still transacting outside of the system in real-time.' Civil servant salary payments are partly digital but large-scale G2P social transfers have not fully transitioned. Government tax and revenue collection via Msonkho Online is growing but compliance remains a challenge. Overall government digital payment adoption is estimated below 20%.

Definition: Whether refugees, asylum seekers, internally displaced persons, migrants, and stateless persons can legally access and open digital payment accounts, and practical barriers or enablers for these populations.
Comments: Refugee and migrant access to digital payments is partial in Malawi. Centenary Bank operates a branch at the Dzaleka refugee camp (hosting ~49,000 refugees) where 17,420 customer accounts have been opened for refugees, enabling banking, WFP cash transfers, and remittances. Refugees can access accounts using UNHCR proof of registration and camp-issued IDs. However, obtaining a registered SIM card for mobile money typically requires a national ID, which many refugees lack. MACRA conducted a SIM card re-registration exercise in 2025 requiring verified registration. Access is therefore partial: some formal banking is available via specialised initiatives (Dzaleka), but mainstream mobile money access via SIM registration faces barriers for those without national identity documents.
